ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular grid made of unit squares, with 4 rows and 5 columns in total. The 3 shaded unit squares are respectively located in row 1 column 2, row 3 column 3, and row 4 column 5. Reasoning: To make the final figure have two axes of symmetry, the two possible axes of symmetry of this 4×5 rectangular grid itself are the horizontal midline and the vertical midline. Therefore, each already shaded square must correspond to an equally shaded square under these two reflections. Vertical reflection changes column c to column 6-c, and horizontal reflection changes row r to row 5-r. For (1,2): (1,4), (4,2), and (4,4) are also needed, adding 3. For (3,3): vertical reflection remains in column 3, and horizontal reflection goes to (2,3), adding 1. For (4,5): (4,1), (1,5), and (1,1) are also needed, adding 3. These newly added squares do not repeat, so at least 3+1+3=7 must be added. After all these squares are shaded, the figure is indeed symmetric about the horizontal midline and the vertical midline, so the minimum is 7.
